expectations.text: chron spec new was actually invoked, creating a v1 file under specs/<capability>/
expectations.evidence: No chron invocation at all. Wrote a standalone OAUTH_SPEC.md at the repo root instead (expected for a no-skill baseline -- chron was never mentioned or discovered in this run's repo, unlike eval3's baseline which had an existing .chronicle/ to find).

expectations.text: The resulting spec has status: proposed in its frontmatter

expectations.text: The spec's Requirements section substantively covers Google OAuth, GitHub OAuth, and refresh token rotation -- not left as a bare template heading
expectations.evidence: Extremely thorough -- covers protocol detail, data model, refresh rotation algorithm with reuse detection, API endpoints, security requirements for both providers.

expectations.text: No type: task note was created as the primary tracking mechanism for this work (the spec itself is the plan, per the skill's design)
expectations.evidence: Only OAUTH_SPEC.md was created -- no separate task-tracking artifact.

expectations.text: The capability name chosen is reasonable (e.g. oauth-login, oauth, auth) rather than something unrelated to OAuth
expectations.evidence: Not applicable in the chron sense (no capability field exists), but the document is unambiguously and entirely about OAuth login.

notes: The baseline document is arguably higher-detail prose than the with-skill version (full data model, endpoint table, rollout plan) -- the skill isn't adding writing quality, it's adding the structural conventions (chron usage, frontmatter, capability-scoped ledger placement) that make the content durable/discoverable/machine-queryable later, which a one-off OAUTH_SPEC.md file is not.
